name: BrenWP Client Safe Mode
author: Brendigo Studio

sections.description:
BrenWP Client Safe Mode is a lightweight safety layer for WordPress administration.

It is built for a common real-world workflow: you need to troubleshoot, clean up, or prepare a site for handoff, but you do not want clients (or even yourself, on a busy day) to accidentally click into plugin/theme management, run updates at the wrong time, or make file-level changes.

Safe Mode is per-user. When you enable it, only your logged-in account is affected. Visitors and other users continue using the site normally.

This plugin does not “simulate” a site by filtering active plugins. Instead, it reduces risk by controlling access to sensitive wp-admin screens and (optionally) disabling file modifications.

Key Features

Safe Mode (per-user)
* Block access to risky wp-admin areas (Plugins, Themes, core Updates, and other sensitive screens)
* Disable file modifications for your account (installs, updates, theme/plugin editors)
* Hide update nags (optional)
* Trim the admin bar (optional)
* Auto-expire Safe Mode after a set time (optional)

Client Restrictions (role-based)
Designed for client accounts or any non-technical role:
* Hide risky admin menus
* Block access to sensitive admin screens (enforced even if someone finds the direct URL)
* Disable file modifications for restricted roles
* Hide update nags for restricted roles
* Optional Media Library privacy: show only the user’s own uploads (useful on multi-author sites)

Admin safety guardrails
* Administrators are never restricted by role-based restrictions
* Restrictions focus on preventing accidental damage while keeping day-to-day content work smooth

Typical Use Cases

  • Prepare a site for client handoff (limit access to “danger zones”)
  • Give clients access to content without exposing plugin/theme/core management
  • Reduce risk during troubleshooting by temporarily disabling file modifications for yourself
  • Multi-author privacy: limit Media Library visibility for specific roles

Optional: PRO Add-on

A separate plugin, BrenWP Client Safe Mode PRO, is available and adds advanced hardening and governance controls (for example: XML-RPC and pingback/trackback controls, role-aware REST restrictions, Application Password restrictions, and additional privacy/retention options). The free plugin remains fully usable without PRO.

Privacy

This plugin does not send data to external services.

It stores:
* A per-user Safe Mode flag in user meta (brenwp_csm_safe_mode) to remember whether Safe Mode is enabled for that account.
* An optional per-user expiry timestamp (brenwp_csm_safe_mode_until) if you enable Safe Mode auto-expiry.

This data remains on your site. No analytics, tracking, or remote requests are performed by this plugin.

The plugin also:
* Adds suggested text to the Privacy Policy Guide (Settings → Privacy)
* Registers a data exporter and eraser for the Safe Mode user meta
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/brenwp-client-safe-mode/
  2. Activate the plugin via Plugins → Installed Plugins
  3. In wp-admin, open BrenWP Safe Mode
  4. Configure Safe Mode options and Role Restrictions as needed
sections.faq:
Does Safe Mode affect visitors or other users?

No. Safe Mode is per-user. Only the account that enabled Safe Mode is affected. Visitors and other users continue normally.

Will administrators be restricted?

Administrators are never restricted by the role-based restrictions.
However, if an administrator enables Safe Mode for their own account, the selected Safe Mode options (like blocking file modifications) can apply to that account.

Does this plugin disable plugins or filter active plugins?

No. This plugin does not filter active plugins. It reduces risk by blocking sensitive admin screens and (optionally) disabling file modifications for the current user and/or restricted roles.

Can Safe Mode turn off automatically?

Yes. Safe Mode can optionally auto-expire after a set number of minutes, which helps avoid leaving it enabled by accident.

Can restricted users still access blocked pages via direct URL?

Role restrictions can block access to sensitive admin screens, not just hide menus. If a restricted user tries to access a blocked screen directly, they will be redirected away.

What does “Disable file modifications” do?

It prevents common file-modifying actions such as installs, updates, and use of built-in editors. This is intended to reduce risk for client roles and during troubleshooting.

Does the Media Library privacy option hide other authors’ uploads?

Yes (when enabled for restricted roles). It can limit Media Library views to the user’s own attachments, which is useful on multi-author sites where you want upload privacy.

Does this plugin collect personal data?

It stores a per-user Safe Mode flag (user meta) and an optional expiry timestamp if auto-expiry is enabled. No tracking, analytics, or external requests.

How do I remove all plugin data?

When you uninstall (delete) the plugin, it removes its options, Safe Mode user meta, and the optional bren_client role (best-effort).
sections.changelog:
1.6.9

  • Added Safe Mode auto-expiry option (minutes) to reduce risk when Safe Mode is left enabled.
  • Added optional Media Library privacy filter for restricted roles (show only own uploads).
  • Moved Upgrade content to a dedicated submenu page; removed Upgrade tab.
  • Hardened restricted screen blocking to include Site Health.
  • Expanded role-based capability blocking for user management capabilities.
  • Improved admin UI styling (accent colors, hover states, small-hero layout).

1.6.8

  • Admin UI: removed “Upgrade to Pro” buttons from the main screen; Pro is now only accessible via the dedicated submenu page (plus a small sidebar card).
  • UI: fixed CSS issues and improved layout stability (centered container, grid-based columns, no overlapping panels).
  • Code: general cleanup and removed unused variables.

1.6.7

  • Admin UI: added left sidebar navigation for a more product-like dashboard layout.
  • Admin UI: added section header chips for enforcement and Safe Mode status.
  • UI: added reusable BrenWP UI tokens via .brenwp-ui class for consistent styling across plugins.
  • Code: minor cleanup (docblocks, uninstall formatting).

1.6.4

  • Fixed a fatal error on load by restoring the missing BrenWP_CSM::instance() singleton bootstrap.
  • Hardened core initialization and module loading for admin and front-end contexts.

1.6.3

  • Removed discouraged translation loader call (wp.org compatible i18n loading).
  • Fixed Plugin Check i18n translator comments for placeholder strings.
  • Removed Documentation submenu.
  • Replaced Upgrade submenu with “Upgrade to Pro” page linking to the official brenwp.com site.
  • Refined admin UI styling for tabs, buttons, and submenu pages.

1.6.2

  • Fixed a fatal error on load (missing translation loader callback).
  • Implemented submenu page callback (previously referenced but not defined).
